questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics' delivery confirmation always uses the exact same layout. Which document type should their custom model use?
questions.explain: Fixed template documents is designed for forms where fields consistently land in the same place, and it trains more quickly than General documents.

questions.q: Which four kinds of items can a document processing model be taught to extract?
options: Text fields, number fields, date fields, checkboxes, and tables
questions.explain: You define text, number, and date fields, checkboxes, and tables (with named columns) on the 'Choose information to extract' screen.

questions.q: What is the current name of the flow action that runs a document processing model, as of May 2025?
questions.explain: The action was renamed from 'Extract information from documents' to 'Process documents' in May 2025 — same action, same behavior.

questions.q: A tagged field comes back from the model with a confidence score of 0.22. What should that low score tell you to do?
options: Trust the value automatically since it still returned something
Ignore confidence scores entirely — they don't matter
Treat it as a signal to route the document to a human reviewer instead of acting on the value blindly
questions.explain: A low confidence score means the model isn't sure about the extracted value, which is exactly the kind of case that should be routed for human review rather than automated on.

questions.q: When a document processing model extracts a table with multiple rows, how does Power Automate typically handle the action that uses those column values?
options: It fails unless you manually add a loop
It automatically wraps that action in an Apply to each, since a table can have any number of rows
It only ever returns the first row
It converts the table into a single text field
questions.explain: Because a table can contain any number of rows, Power Automate automatically wraps the action using a table's column values in an Apply to each control.
